messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 Paging: Production spike detected - inference-api-01 5xx rate > 4% for 3m. Error signature: kvcache eviction OOM in runtime v2.3. Triggered by recent canary deploy (sha: a1b2c3d).
Maya: on it. I'm the oncall for the hour. Switching to incident channel.
Tom: I can see the same trace in logs, memory grows on sequence start when kvcache.reset runs. That commit a1b2c3d touched cache eviction logic.
Maya: Can we kill the feature flag for the canary region (eu-west-1) first? If kill reduces error, we avoid a full rollback. Who can flip it?
Priya: I have access to FF dashboard. Flipping flag now: feature.new_kvcache_eviction -> off for eu-west-1.
DeployBot: :white_check_mark: feature.new_kvcache_eviction disabled in eu-west-1 (actor=Priya). Canary traffic should shift within 30s.
Maya: Monitoring metrics… 60s… 120s… 5xx still slightly elevated but trending down. Looks like partial reduction.
Tom: Hmm, looks like some nodes already pulled the new binary. We should still prepare a fast revert of the single offending commit. I'll open a revert PR and cut a hotfix build.
Tom: Revert commands I'm running locally:
```
git checkout main
git pull origin main
git revert --no-edit a1b2c3d
git push origin HEAD:hotfix/revert-a1b2c3d
```
Then creating PR and tagging @deploy for expedited CI.
Maya: Good. If revert passes CI, we want a single-commit patch release to Dedicated and Hosted canaries, then promote. Keep canary at 10% traffic.
Tom: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/987 (title: revert: kvcache eviction change a1b2c3d). CI triggered with priority pipeline.
DeployBot: :rocket: CI passed for hotfix/revert-a1b2c3d. Ready for canary deploy.
Maya: Proceeding to deploy hotfix to canary pool (10%). Tom coordinate with SRE for rollout plan.
Tom: Deploy commands (internal):
```
redwood deploy promote --service=runtime --image-tag=hotfix-revert-a1b2c3d --strategy=canary --batch=10%
```
Starting deploy now.
Maya: Watching logs and 5xx. Priya, please prepare customer-impact note in #customer-success if we need to alert.
Priya: Making draft: "We observed transient 5xx errors in the eu-west region after a recent deployment; we've rolled back the change and are monitoring. No data loss. Will update within 30m."
Maya: 3m post-hotfix canary: 5xx back to baseline. Good. Keep canary running 15m then promote.
Tom: After 12m of stable canary I'm promoting to 50% then full.
DeployBot: :white_check_mark: Hotfix promoted to 50% canary (timestamp=1951234880).
Maya: 5xx stable at baseline across regions. Initiating final promote to 100%.
DeployBot: :white_check_mark: Hotfix promoted to 100% (timestamp=1951234965). All canaries healthy.
Maya: Great. Priya, send the CS update and mark customers impacted: small subset in eu-west on inference-api-01; list of org ids observed attached.
Priya: Sent update in #customer-success and started a support blurb. No major SLA breaches; will offer postmortem if customers request.
Tom: Recording deploy notes and linking PR/commit in incident doc. Action item: add a guard in kvcache to cap memory growth on input size, and add unit test for eviction race.
Jun: I'm up next oncall in 30m. Maya, handoff notes?
Maya: Handoff: incident resolved, root cause correlative to commit a1b2c3d which changed eviction timing. Hotfix revert deployed globally. Monitoring good. Followups: postmortem, add regression test, consider stronger feature-flag gating for eviction experiments.
Maya: Passing to Jun for watch. If anything resurfaces ping me.
Jun: Ack, I'll monitor for the window and will start the postmortem doc.
Maya: Thanks all. Closing slack coordination — creating incident ticket: INC-2026-141 with timeline and links.
incident-bot: Incident channel update: incident resolved (severity=sev2), responders: Maya, Tom, Priya.
Maya: Adding short note: quick revert approach worked well. Recommend we standardize single-commit hotfix playbook for runtime changes.
Tom: Agreed. I'll draft the hotfix playbook and paste the commands + checklist into the incident ticket.
Priya: I'll coordinate the customer follow-ups and keep CS looped for any requests.
Maya: End of thread.
